horses.incident_text: L Hewitson stated that the horse travelled satisfactorily in the early stages but when asked for an effort in the Home Straight failed to respond.  He added, in his opinion, the horse may be better suited down in grade.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings. <2/3/2026 Additional Veterinary Reports> WIN SPEED, which performed disappointingly, was examined by the Veterinary Officer who said at that time there were no significant findings. WIN SPEED was again examined by the Veterinary Officer at the stables of Trainer B Crawford this morning. He said at this time he noted the horse to be lame in its right front leg. Before being allowed to race again, WIN SPEED will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

L Hewitson stated that his mount failed to respond to his riding in the Home Straight and was disappointing.  Trainer M Newnham confirmed that with the horse dropping back from 1400 Metres to 1200 Metres today Jockey Hewitson was obliged to make some use of the horse in the early stages to go forward and, in his opinion, this was the reason why it was not able to finish off in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

M F Poon reported that the intention was to find a midfield position with cover.  He said when ORIGIN OF FORM jumped well he was able to hold an on-pace position but was obliged to race wide and without cover for the majority of the event.

When questioned H Bowman stated that he was instructed to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages to ensure that it ran out a strong 2000 Metres.  He added whilst he had expected to settle back in the field he had not anticipated the race being run inside of standard time in the early and middle stages.  He said near the 500 Metres he commenced to shift to the outside of WINNING WING, however, when that runner shifted out at the same point he then elected to save ground and improve to the inside of WINNING WING near the 450 Metres whereby MY WISH responded well to his riding.  He said after making good ground between the 400 Metres and the 150 Metres the horse’s run ended which he attributed to the early and middle stages of the race being run inside of standard time.  Trainer M Newnham confirmed the instructions and stated he issued those instructions to allow the horse to run out a strong 2000 Metres.

Was examined by the Veterinary Officer after arriving at the Start at the request of Jockey Z Purton and passed suitable to race.  When questioned Z Purton stated that the horse travelled satisfactorily during the race and he was comfortable with the early and middle stages being run inside of standard time as the horse had performed well when it won over 2400 Metres previously on a strong pace.  He added VOYAGE BUBBLE came under pressure prior to entering the Home Straight and did not respond to his riding and was disappointing.  He said after the event the horse appeared to pull up satisfactorily.  Assistant Trainer H F Yiu representing Trainer P F Yiu stated that the horse had pleased the stable coming into today’s race and he could offer no explanation for its performance.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

When questioned B Avdulla stated that from barrier 2 and when the connections were of the opinion there was not strong pace in the event he was given the option to lead if BEAUTY JOY jumped well.  He said as a result when his mount commenced well he elected to allow the horse to stride forward and lead the event.  He added that BEAUTY JOY raced keenly throughout the early and middle stages and as a result ran inside of standard time despite his efforts to set a more sustainable pace.  He said due to the manner the horse raced throughout the early and middle stages it did not respond to his riding in the Home Straight.  Trainer A S Cruz confirmed that he had given B Avdulla the option to go forward.  He said he issued those instructions as BEAUTY JOY has been finishing its races off only fairly due to racing keenly in the early stages when settling back in the field.
Sent for sampling post-race.

Bumped on jumping.  R Kingscote stated that whilst he expected to hold a forward position he was given the option of obtaining cover if circumstances permitted.  He said when PAKISTAN LEGACY showed the intent to lead the event he allowed that runner to cross him and obtain a position with cover behind that horse.  Assistant Trainer H F Yiu representing Trainer P F Yiu confirmed the instructions and stated that at its last start on 25 January 2026 the horse was disadvantaged by taking on for the lead and as a result he had given Jockey Kingscote the option to ride it with cover.  Sent for sampling post-race.

M Guyon was advised to ensure that there is sufficient racing room when improving into runs.  LUCY IN THE SKY was then shifted to the inside of SUPERB KING and near the 150 Metres was steadied when disappointed for clear running between SUPERB KING and GENEVA (H Bowman) which shifted out. When questioned K C Leung stated that his instructions were to lead.  He said in the early stages along the Back Straight he remained wide and allowed his mount time to move forward and to race in the lead.  He said after improving to the outside of AKASHVANI near the 1000 Metres, when that runner did not show the intent to hold the lead, he elected to allow NUMBERS to stride forward to cross AKASHVANI and lead as instructed.  When questioned regarding his riding from the 800 Metres and if there was an opportunity to set a slower pace K C Leung stated that as NUMBERS is a big striding horse and one-paced he was satisfied that the horse was racing in a comfortable rhythm and as a result he elected to allow it to continue to stride forward without restraining his mount as he felt it would provide it with the best opportunity to obtain the best possible placing in the race.

horses.short: Must pass veterinary exam before racing again
horses.incident_text: After travelling a short distance was crowded for room between JUNEAU PRIDE and HEALTHY HAPPY which shifted out slightly.  M F Poon reported that he had concerns with his mount’s action during the race.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  Before being allowed to race again, MR ASCENDENCY will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

L Hewitson stated that his mount jumped only fairly and when the pace of the event was run inside of standard time in the early stages he elected to take a position with cover.  He added that the horse failed to respond to his riding in the Home Straight and, in his opinion, is better suited on the All Weather surface.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
